title: The Cardinality Gap: from ℚ to the Continuum Hypothesis
content: Develops the full cardinality landscape from the denumerability of $\mathbb{Q}$. Starting from $|\mathbb{Q}| = \aleph_0$ (parent file), this entry proves $|\mathbb{R}| = \mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$, establishes $|\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})| = \mathfrak{c}$ (the Dedekind cut connection), proves $\aleph_1 \le \mathfrak{c}$, and formalizes the Continuum Hypothesis and its independence from ZFC. Cantor posed CH in 1878; Hilbert listed it as Problem 1 in 1900; Gödel (1940) and Cohen (1963) established independence.
mathContext: The chain: $\aleph_0 = |\mathbb{Q}| < |\mathbb{R}| = \mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$. CH: $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$, equivalently $\nexists \kappa: \aleph_0 < \kappa < \mathfrak{c}$. Independence: CH is consistent with ZFC (Gödel, via $L$) and $\neg$CH is also consistent (Cohen, via forcing).

title: Cardinality of ℚ and ℝ from Mathlib
content: Establishes the base facts: $|\mathbb{Q}| = \aleph_0$ (from Mathlib's `Denumerable ℚ` instance, which provides an explicit bijection $\mathbb{N} \simeq \mathbb{Q}$ via Cantor pairing) and $|\mathbb{R}| = \mathfrak{c}$ (from Mathlib's `mk_real`). Proves $|\mathbb{Q}| < |\mathbb{R}|$ by rewriting to $\aleph_0 < \mathfrak{c}$ and applying Cantor's theorem. Notably, $\mathbb{Q}$ is dense in $\mathbb{R}$ yet strictly smaller—density is a topological property independent of cardinality.
mathContext: $|\mathbb{Q}| = \aleph_0$ because $\mathbb{Q} \cong \mathbb{Z} \times \mathbb{Z}_{>0} / \sim$ (fractions $p/q$ in lowest terms), and $\mathbb{Z}^2$ is countable. $|\mathbb{R}| = 2^{\aleph_0}$ because $\mathbb{R} \cong \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}}$ via binary expansions (with care for dyadic rationals).

title: The Dedekind Cut Connection: |𝒫(ℚ)| = 𝔠
content: Proves that the power set of $\mathbb{Q}$ has continuum cardinality: $|\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})| = 2^{|\mathbb{Q}|} = 2^{\aleph_0} = \mathfrak{c}$. This connects the denumerability of $\mathbb{Q}$ to the size of $\mathbb{R}$: each Dedekind cut is a subset of $\mathbb{Q}$, so $\mathbb{R}$ embeds into $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})$, which has the same cardinality as $\mathbb{R}$ itself. The paradox: $\mathbb{Q}$ is 'small' (countable) but $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})$ is 'large' (continuum-sized).
mathContext: Cantor's theorem: $|X| < |\mathcal{P}(X)|$ for any set $X$. Applied to $\mathbb{Q}$: $\aleph_0 = |\mathbb{Q}| < |\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})| = 2^{\aleph_0} = \mathfrak{c}$. The Dedekind cut map $\iota: \mathbb{R} \hookrightarrow \mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})$, $r \mapsto \{q \in \mathbb{Q} : q < r\}$, gives $|\mathbb{R}| \le |\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})|$, and the reverse holds since $\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q}) \hookrightarrow \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{Q}} \cong \{0,1\}^{\mathbb{N}} \cong \mathbb{R}$.

title: The Aleph Hierarchy and ℵ₁ ≤ 𝔠
content: Establishes the aleph hierarchy bounds provable in ZFC: $\aleph_0 < \mathfrak{c}$ (Cantor), $\aleph_0 < \aleph_1$ (successor cardinal definition), and $\aleph_1 \le \mathfrak{c}$ (since $\aleph_1$ is the smallest cardinal exceeding $\aleph_0$, and $\mathfrak{c}$ also exceeds $\aleph_0$). The proof of $\aleph_0 < \aleph_1$ uses `Cardinal.aleph_lt_aleph` and simplification. The bound $\aleph_1 \le \mathfrak{c}$ is the strongest statement ZFC can make about the relationship—CH asks whether equality holds.
mathContext: $\aleph_1 = \min\{\kappa : \kappa > \aleph_0\}$ is the successor cardinal. In ZFC: $\aleph_0 < \aleph_1 \le \mathfrak{c} = 2^{\aleph_0}$. CH asserts $\aleph_1 = \mathfrak{c}$; under $\neg$CH, $\aleph_1 < \mathfrak{c}$ and the actual value of $\mathfrak{c}$ among the alephs is undetermined (it could be $\aleph_2$, $\aleph_{\omega}$, or even larger, subject to König's theorem: $\text{cf}(\mathfrak{c}) > \aleph_0$).

title: Continuum Hypothesis: Equivalence of Formulations
content: Defines CH as $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$ and the gap formulation as $\nexists \kappa: \aleph_0 < \kappa < \mathfrak{c}$. Proves their equivalence `ch_equiv_no_intermediate` by showing: (forward) if $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1 = \text{succ}(\aleph_0)$, any $\kappa$ with $\kappa < \text{succ}(\aleph_0)$ satisfies $\kappa \le \aleph_0$, contradicting $\kappa > \aleph_0$; (backward) if no intermediate exists, $\aleph_1 \le \mathfrak{c}$ and $\neg(\aleph_1 < \mathfrak{c})$ (else $\aleph_1$ would be intermediate), giving $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$.
mathContext: CH: $\mathfrak{c} = \aleph_1$, equivalently $2^{\aleph_0} = \aleph_1$, equivalently $\nexists S \subseteq \mathbb{R}: \aleph_0 < |S| < \mathfrak{c}$. The proof of equivalence uses the successor property: $\aleph_1 = \text{succ}(\aleph_0)$, so $\kappa < \aleph_1 \Leftrightarrow \kappa \le \aleph_0$.

title: CH Implications: The Cardinality Landscape Under CH and ¬CH
content: Under CH, the infinite cardinal landscape below 𝔠 collapses: only ℵ₀ and 𝔠 exist (proved via ch_only_two_infinite_cardinals_le_continuum). Under ¬CH, at least one intermediate cardinal exists between ℵ₀ and 𝔠, specifically ℵ₁ < 𝔠 (proved via not_ch_implies_aleph1_lt_continuum). The ¬CH case is dramatically more complex: Easton's theorem shows 𝔠 could be ℵ₂, ℵ₃, ℵ_ω₁, or much larger, subject only to König's cofinality constraint cf(𝔠) > ℵ₀.
mathContext: Under CH: $\{\kappa : \aleph_0 \le \kappa \le \mathfrak{c}\} = \{\aleph_0, \mathfrak{c}\}$. Under $\neg$CH: $\aleph_1 < \mathfrak{c}$, so $\aleph_1$ is an intermediate cardinal. Easton: for any function $F$ on regular cardinals with $\text{cf}(F(\kappa)) > \kappa$, there is a model of ZFC where $2^\kappa = F(\kappa)$.

title: Independence of CH and Summary
content: Axiomatizes the independence of CH: `godel_ch_consistent_with_ZFC` (Gödel 1940, via the constructible universe $L$) and `cohen_not_ch_consistent_with_ZFC` (Cohen 1963, via forcing). Combines them into `ch_independent_of_ZFC`. The summary theorem `denumerability_to_ch_summary` packages all ZFC-provable facts: $|\mathbb{Q}| = \aleph_0$, $|\mathbb{R}| = \mathfrak{c}$, $|\mathbb{Q}| < |\mathbb{R}|$, $|\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{Q})| = \mathfrak{c}$, and $\aleph_1 \le \mathfrak{c}$.
mathContext: Gödel (1940) showed $\text{Con}(\text{ZFC}) \Rightarrow \text{Con}(\text{ZFC} + \text{CH})$ by constructing the minimal model $L$ (constructible sets). Cohen (1963) showed $\text{Con}(\text{ZFC}) \Rightarrow \text{Con}(\text{ZFC} + \neg\text{CH})$ by adjoining generic reals via forcing. Together: CH is independent of ZFC. Cohen received the Fields Medal in 1966.
